chapters.title: Foundations of AI, ML & Deep Learning
chapters.description: Complete understanding of Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning, and Deep Learning fundamentals

pages.title: What is Artificial Intelligence?
pages.content: Artificial Intelligence (AI) refers to the simulation of human intelligence in machines. It enables machines to think, reason, learn, and make decisions. AI systems can perform tasks such as speech recognition, decision-making, visual perception, and language translation.
keyPoints: Used in automation and decision making

pages.title: Machine Learning Explained
pages.content: Machine Learning (ML) is a subset of AI that allows systems to learn from data without being explicitly programmed. ML models improve performance as they are exposed to more data.
pages.exampleCode:
from sklearn.linear_model import LinearRegression
model = LinearRegression()

pages.title: Types of Machine Learning
pages.content: Machine Learning has three main types: Supervised Learning (labeled data), Unsupervised Learning (no labels), and Reinforcement Learning (reward-based learning).

pages.title: Introduction to Deep Learning
pages.content: Deep Learning is a subset of ML that uses neural networks with multiple layers. It is used in complex tasks like image recognition, NLP, and speech processing.

pages.title: Applications of AI
pages.content: AI is used in healthcare, finance, education, automation, chatbots, recommendation systems, and more.

chapters.title: Introduction to Generative AI
chapters.description: Deep dive into generative AI concepts, models, and applications

pages.title: What is Generative AI?
pages.content: Generative AI refers to systems that can generate new content such as text, images, audio, video, and code. These models learn patterns from existing data and create similar but new outputs.
keyPoints: Core of ChatGPT and image AI

pages.title: Generative vs Predictive AI
pages.content: Predictive AI predicts outcomes based on input data, while Generative AI creates new outputs such as text, images, or music.

pages.title: Types of Generative Models
pages.content: Generative AI includes models such as GANs (image generation), VAEs (probability-based models), Transformers (text generation), and Diffusion models (high-quality image generation).

pages.title: Real-World Applications
pages.content: Generative AI is used in chatbots, image generation, code assistants, video creation, content writing, and AI interview systems.

pages.title: Limitations of Generative AI
pages.content: Generative AI can produce hallucinations (incorrect outputs), bias, and security risks. It requires careful design and evaluation.

chapters.title: Neural Networks & Deep Learning
chapters.description: Detailed understanding of neural networks, layers, and training process

pages.title: What is a Neural Network?
pages.content: A neural network is a system inspired by the human brain that processes data through layers of interconnected nodes (neurons).

pages.title: Perceptron Model
pages.content: A perceptron is the simplest form of a neural network that takes inputs, applies weights, and produces output.

pages.title: Activation Functions
pages.content: Activation functions determine whether a neuron should be activated. Common ones include ReLU, Sigmoid, and Tanh.

pages.title: Forward & Backpropagation
pages.content: Forward propagation computes outputs, while backpropagation updates weights based on error.

pages.title: Training Neural Networks
pages.content: Training involves feeding data, calculating loss, and updating weights using optimizers like Gradient Descent.

chapters.title: Transformers Architecture
chapters.description: In-depth understanding of transformer models, attention mechanism, and architecture behind modern LLMs

pages.title: Introduction to Transformers
pages.content: Transformers are deep learning models designed to process sequential data efficiently. Unlike RNNs, transformers process all inputs in parallel, making them faster and more scalable.

pages.title: Self-Attention Mechanism
pages.content: Self-attention allows the model to focus on important words in a sentence by assigning weights to each token.

pages.title: Query, Key, Value Explained
pages.content: Each word is converted into Query, Key, and Value vectors. The attention mechanism compares queries with keys to compute importance.

pages.title: Multi-Head Attention
pages.content: Multi-head attention allows the model to focus on different parts of the sentence simultaneously.

pages.title: Positional Encoding
pages.content: Transformers do not process data sequentially, so positional encoding is used to give information about token positions.

pages.title: Encoder-Decoder Architecture
pages.content: Transformers consist of encoders (process input) and decoders (generate output).

pages.title: Applications of Transformers
pages.content: Transformers are used in chatbots, translation, summarization, and code generation.

chapters.title: Large Language Models (LLMs)
chapters.description: Deep understanding of LLMs, training process, and working of models like GPT

pages.title: What are Large Language Models?
pages.content: LLMs are deep learning models trained on massive text datasets to understand and generate human-like language.

pages.title: How LLMs are Trained
pages.content: LLMs are trained using self-supervised learning where the model predicts the next word in a sentence.

pages.title: Tokenization in LLMs
pages.content: Text is broken into tokens before processing. Tokens can be words, subwords, or characters.

pages.title: Context Window
pages.content: Context window defines how much text the model can remember at once.

pages.title: Fine-Tuning vs Pretraining
pages.content: Pretraining is done on large datasets, while fine-tuning adapts the model for specific tasks.

pages.title: Popular LLMs
pages.content: Popular models include GPT, BERT, LLaMA, and Claude.

pages.title: Limitations of LLMs
pages.content: LLMs may produce incorrect or biased outputs and require careful usage.

chapters.title: Tokenization & Embeddings
chapters.description: Understanding how text is converted into numerical representations for AI models

pages.title: What is Tokenization?
pages.content: Tokenization is the process of splitting text into smaller units called tokens.

pages.title: Types of Tokenization
pages.content: Tokenization types include word-level, character-level, and subword tokenization.

pages.title: What are Embeddings?
pages.content: Embeddings convert text into numerical vectors that represent meaning.

pages.title: Word Embeddings vs Sentence Embeddings
pages.content: Word embeddings represent individual words, while sentence embeddings represent full sentences.

pages.title: Similarity Search
pages.content: Embeddings allow similarity comparison using cosine similarity.

pages.title: Embedding Models
pages.content: Models like OpenAI embeddings, Word2Vec, and Sentence Transformers generate embeddings.

pages.title: Applications of Embeddings
pages.content: Embeddings are used in search engines, recommendation systems, chatbots, and semantic search.

chapters.title: Prompt Engineering (Advanced)
chapters.description: Mastering advanced prompt design techniques to control and optimize LLM outputs

pages.title: What is Prompt Engineering?
pages.content: Prompt engineering is the process of designing effective inputs to guide AI models toward desired outputs. It plays a critical role in improving accuracy and relevance.
pages.exampleCode: prompt = 'Explain recursion with examples in Python'

pages.title: Zero-Shot Prompting
pages.content: Zero-shot prompting involves giving instructions without any examples.
pages.exampleCode: Translate this sentence to French: Hello

pages.title: Few-Shot Prompting
pages.content: Few-shot prompting includes examples to guide the model.

pages.title: Chain-of-Thought Prompting
pages.content: Encourages models to think step-by-step before answering.

pages.title: Role-Based Prompting
pages.content: Assigning roles to AI improves output quality.
pages.exampleCode: You are a senior software engineer. Explain system design.

pages.title: Prompt Structuring Techniques
pages.content: Structuring prompts with instructions, constraints, and examples yields better results.

pages.title: Advanced Prompt Patterns
pages.content: Patterns include ReAct, Tree-of-Thought, and multi-step reasoning prompts.

pages.title: Prompt Optimization
pages.content: Iteratively refining prompts improves output performance.

chapters.title: Fine-Tuning Models
chapters.description: Customizing large language models using domain-specific data

pages.title: What is Fine-Tuning?
pages.content: Fine-tuning is the process of training a pre-trained model on specific datasets to adapt it for particular tasks.

pages.title: Pretraining vs Fine-Tuning
pages.content: Pretraining uses large datasets, while fine-tuning uses smaller, task-specific datasets.

pages.title: Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT)
pages.content: SFT involves training models using labeled input-output pairs.

pages.title: Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (RLHF)
pages.content: RLHF improves models using human feedback to rank outputs.

pages.title: Dataset Preparation
pages.content: Preparing clean, high-quality datasets is crucial for fine-tuning success.

pages.title: Training Process
pages.content: Fine-tuning involves epochs, loss calculation, and optimization.

pages.title: Challenges in Fine-Tuning
pages.content: Fine-tuning can be expensive and requires large compute resources.

chapters.title: LoRA & PEFT (Efficient Fine-Tuning)
chapters.description: Efficient techniques for fine-tuning large models with minimal resources

pages.title: What is PEFT?
pages.content: Parameter Efficient Fine-Tuning (PEFT) reduces the number of trainable parameters, making fine-tuning more efficient.

pages.title: Introduction to LoRA
pages.content: LoRA (Low-Rank Adaptation) modifies only a small subset of parameters instead of the full model.

pages.title: How LoRA Works
pages.content: LoRA injects trainable low-rank matrices into the model layers.

pages.title: Advantages of LoRA
pages.content: LoRA reduces training cost and memory usage significantly.

pages.title: Other PEFT Techniques
pages.content: Other techniques include adapters, prefix tuning, and prompt tuning.

pages.title: When to Use LoRA vs Fine-Tuning
pages.content: LoRA is preferred when resources are limited, while full fine-tuning is used for maximum accuracy.

pages.title: Real-World Use Cases
pages.content: LoRA is used in chatbots, domain-specific assistants, and enterprise AI systems.

chapters.title: Vector Databases & Semantic Search
chapters.description: Understanding vector databases, embeddings storage, and semantic similarity search systems

pages.title: What is a Vector Database?
pages.content: A vector database stores data in the form of embeddings (numerical vectors) instead of traditional rows and columns. It is optimized for similarity search.
keyPoints: Faster than traditional DB for similarity

pages.title: Traditional DB vs Vector DB
pages.content: Traditional databases use exact matching, while vector databases use similarity matching.

pages.title: Embeddings Storage
pages.content: Embeddings are stored as high-dimensional vectors that represent semantic meaning.

pages.title: Similarity Search
pages.content: Similarity search finds vectors closest to the query using metrics like cosine similarity.

pages.title: Popular Vector Databases
pages.content: Popular vector databases include Pinecone, Weaviate, FAISS, and Milvus.

pages.title: Indexing Techniques
pages.content: Vector databases use indexing techniques like HNSW and IVF for fast retrieval.

pages.title: Use Cases of Vector Databases
pages.content: Used in chatbots, recommendation systems, semantic search, and AI assistants.

chapters.title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG)
chapters.description: Combining vector search with LLMs to build accurate and context-aware AI systems

pages.title: What is RAG?
pages.content: RAG combines retrieval systems with language models to generate responses based on external knowledge.

pages.title: Why RAG is Important
pages.content: RAG helps overcome LLM limitations by providing real-time data and context.

pages.title: RAG Architecture
pages.content: RAG consists of embedding model, vector DB, retriever, and LLM generator.

pages.title: RAG Pipeline Step-by-Step
pages.content: Steps include document ingestion, embedding, storage, retrieval, and response generation.

pages.title: Chunking Strategies
pages.content: Large documents are split into smaller chunks for better retrieval.

pages.title: RAG vs Fine-Tuning
pages.content: RAG uses external data, while fine-tuning modifies the model itself.

pages.title: Real-World Applications
pages.content: Used in enterprise chatbots, document Q&A systems, and knowledge assistants.

chapters.title: LangChain Framework
chapters.description: Building production-ready LLM applications using LangChain

pages.title: Introduction to LangChain
pages.content: LangChain is a framework for building applications powered by LLMs using chains, memory, and tools.

pages.title: Chains in LangChain
pages.content: Chains combine multiple steps into a workflow.

pages.title: Prompt Templates
pages.content: Templates standardize prompts for consistent output.

pages.title: Memory in LangChain
pages.content: Memory allows the model to retain context across conversations.

pages.title: Tools & Agents
pages.content: Agents can use external tools like APIs, databases, and calculators.

pages.title: LangChain with RAG
pages.content: LangChain integrates easily with RAG pipelines.

pages.title: Building Applications
pages.content: LangChain is used to build chatbots, assistants, and automation systems.

chapters.title: AI Agents & Autonomous Systems
chapters.description: Understanding AI agents, decision-making systems, and autonomous workflows

pages.title: What are AI Agents?
pages.content: AI agents are systems that can perceive their environment, make decisions, and take actions to achieve specific goals.

pages.title: Components of an Agent
pages.content: Agents consist of perception, reasoning, memory, and action modules.

pages.title: Types of AI Agents
pages.content: Types include reactive agents, goal-based agents, and learning agents.

pages.title: Agents with Tools
pages.content: Agents can use tools like APIs, databases, and search engines to perform tasks.

pages.title: Planning & Reasoning
pages.content: Agents use reasoning techniques like chain-of-thought and planning algorithms.

pages.title: Multi-Agent Systems
pages.content: Multiple agents collaborate to solve complex problems.

pages.title: Real-World Applications
pages.content: Agents are used in automation, robotics, customer support, and AI assistants.

chapters.title: Multimodal AI
chapters.description: Understanding AI systems that process multiple data types like text, images, and audio

pages.title: What is Multimodal AI?
pages.content: Multimodal AI refers to models that can process and generate multiple types of data such as text, images, audio, and video.

pages.title: Text + Image Models
pages.content: Models like CLIP connect text and images for understanding and retrieval.

pages.title: Image Generation Models
pages.content: Models like DALL·E and Stable Diffusion generate images from text prompts.

pages.title: Speech & Audio Models
pages.content: AI models can convert speech to text and generate audio.

pages.title: Video Generation
pages.content: AI can generate and edit videos using generative models.

pages.title: Fusion Techniques
pages.content: Combining multiple modalities improves understanding and performance.

pages.title: Applications of Multimodal AI
pages.content: Used in autonomous vehicles, healthcare, content creation, and assistants.

chapters.title: Diffusion Models & Image Generation
chapters.description: Understanding diffusion models and how AI generates high-quality images

pages.title: What are Diffusion Models?
pages.content: Diffusion models generate data by gradually removing noise from random inputs.

pages.title: Forward Diffusion Process
pages.content: Noise is gradually added to data until it becomes random.

pages.title: Reverse Diffusion Process
pages.content: The model learns to remove noise step by step to reconstruct data.

pages.title: Stable Diffusion
pages.content: Stable Diffusion is a popular model for generating high-quality images efficiently.

pages.title: Latent Space
pages.content: Diffusion models operate in latent space to improve efficiency.

pages.title: Prompting for Image Generation
pages.content: Well-crafted prompts improve image quality and control.
pages.exampleCode: A futuristic city at sunset, ultra realistic

pages.title: Applications of Diffusion Models
pages.content: Used in design, art, gaming, marketing, and film production.

chapters.title: AI Safety & Ethics
chapters.description: Understanding responsible AI usage, risks, and ethical considerations

pages.title: What is AI Safety?
pages.content: AI safety ensures that AI systems behave as intended without causing harm.

pages.title: Bias in AI Models
pages.content: AI models can reflect biases present in training data.

pages.title: Hallucination in LLMs
pages.content: LLMs may generate incorrect or misleading information.

pages.title: AI Alignment
pages.content: Ensuring AI systems follow human values and intentions.

pages.title: Responsible AI Practices
pages.content: Includes transparency, accountability, and fairness in AI systems.

pages.title: Security Risks in AI
pages.content: AI systems can be vulnerable to attacks like prompt injection.

pages.title: Why Evaluation Matters
pages.content: Evaluation helps measure model performance and reliability.

pages.title: Accuracy & Precision
pages.content: Accuracy measures correctness, while precision measures relevance.

pages.title: BLEU & ROUGE Scores
pages.content: Used to evaluate text generation quality.

pages.title: Human Evaluation
pages.content: Human feedback is critical for evaluating AI outputs.

pages.title: Evaluation Challenges
pages.content: Evaluating generative AI is complex due to subjective outputs.

pages.content: Deploying AI models involves exposing them via APIs for real-world use.

pages.title: Cloud Deployment

pages.content: Optimizing models reduces latency and cost.

pages.title: Scaling Strategies

pages.title: Monitoring & Logging
